ground_truth.design_rationale: Genuine, varied contributions with real corroboration and no duplicated text, clustering, or isolation pattern. Uses 3 students (Student P1/P2/P3), not 2, despite the brief's default of 2 -- with only 2 people and no one else in the scenario, any mutual peer_support/peer_feedback mention between them is structurally indistinguishable from Stage 4's mutual-isolation fraud pattern (there is no one available to serve as an 'external' corroborator), and a one-directional-only mention would instead trip Stage 4b's zero-corroborators check on whichever student receives no credit. A 3-person one-way chain of favors (P1 helps P2, P2 helps P3, P3 helps P1) sidesteps both: every student has exactly one real, well-corroborated in-edge, and no pair mentions each other bidirectionally, so neither Stage 4 nor 4b can fire while the corroboration is still completely genuine. Expected result: zero flags from every check.

ground_truth.fraud_pattern: peer inflation -- suspiciously uniform, glowing peer_feedback with thin real contribution evidence behind it
ground_truth.known_scope_gap_relevant_here: peer_feedback record_type is out of scope for Stage 2 (find_cross_student_similar_contributions only scans record_type='contribution' by design, per its own docstring). Student Q1 and Q3's peer_feedback entries are deliberately near-identical superlative wording ('exceptional', 'outstanding') -- a real inflation signal -- but this will NOT be caught by any current check by name, since nothing scans cross-student peer_feedback similarity. This is not a bug being discovered here; it is the pre-documented Stage 2 scope boundary, empirically exercised.
ground_truth.design_rationale: Student Q1 gets uniformly glowing, near-identical peer_feedback (a soft inflation signal, not algorithmically checked) while their actual contributions are thin and generic (README updates, formatting fixes) and their one peer_support claim ('personally resolved every major blocker Q2 faced') is vague/grandiose and does not semantically match anything in Q2's real, substantive, unrelated contribution record -- this is what should trip Stage 1c. Student Q3 shares Q1's glowing-feedback pattern as a second instance (reinforcing that this isn't a one-off). Student Q2 is the contrast case: modest, specific peer_feedback and substantive real contributions, included so the scenario isn't uniformly suspicious.

ground_truth.fraud_pattern: temporal anomaly -- one student's real work is suspiciously clustered in the final 2 days of an otherwise 6-week (42-day) project, despite attending meetings normally throughout
ground_truth.known_gap_being_tested: None of Stages 1/1b/1c/2/4/4b analyze a single student's OWN contribution date distribution for clustering. Stage 1b's check_temporal_plausibility() only checks whether a peer_support CLAIM's date is near the RECIPIENT's own nearby activity (corroboration timing for one claim) -- it never looks at whether a student's overall body of work is suspiciously bunched up. This scenario exists specifically to empirically confirm whether this gap is real, not to assume it.
ground_truth.design_rationale: Student R1 attends meetings on a normal cadence across all 6 weeks (days 3, 15, 30, 38) but logs zero non-meeting contributions until the final 2 days (2026-06-10 and 2026-06-11), where 6 code/task contributions suddenly appear -- a classic last-minute-work pattern. R1's one peer_support claim is deliberately made to genuinely check out (Student R2 has a real, matching contribution corroborating it), so Stage 1c should NOT flag it -- isolating the temporal-clustering signal as the only anomaly in this scenario, uncontaminated by a corroboration failure that would otherwise also explain a flag. Student R2 is a normal baseline with contributions spread evenly across the whole 6 weeks, for contrast.

ground_truth.fraud_pattern: coordinated fraud combining near-duplicate contribution text AND mutual-only corroboration between two students
ground_truth.design_rationale: Student S1 and S2 (only 2 students in this scenario, deliberately, since mutual isolation is the intended positive result here rather than something to avoid) share two pairs of near-identical non-meeting descriptions: a 'login form validation' code entry worded almost verbatim by both, and an identical 'Set up the shared component library' task text -- targeting Stage 2. Their peer_feedback entries both explicitly name the other student ('Formed a strong duo with Student SX...'), reinforcing peer_support's mutual recipient claims, so both source types in build_mention_graph() point the same way: S1<->S2 mutually, with zero mentions from anyone else in this small group -- targeting Stage 4. The peer_support claims themselves are also left uncorroborated by real matching evidence, which may additionally trip Stage 1c; that is expected and consistent with the 'everything at once' design, not a confound to control for.
